finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If 'filename' contains a malicious path or command
finding.assumptions: The 'readFileIntoRawString' function is implemented to execute a command or open a file based on the 'filename' parameter.

parsed.change_summary: No changes were made to the code as the finding does not provide enough information to determine the vulnerability or how to fix it.

parsed.refutation_attempt: 1) Checked the source of the filename variable: it is a hard‑coded string literal "TextFile1.txt" on line 82, not derived from stdin, argv, environment, or any external input. 2) Verified that no other code path assigns a value to filename before the call on line 83. 3) Confirmed that readFileIntoRawString is invoked with a constant argument, so no command injection can occur. 4) No additional checks or sanitisation are required because the source is not untrusted.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If 'output' contains a malicious path or command
finding.assumptions: The 'std::cout' function is implemented to execute a command or open a file based on the 'output' parameter.

parsed.change_summary: Added std::quoted to the std::cout statement to prevent OS Command Injection.
parsed.how_trigger_is_blocked: The trigger is blocked because std::quoted ensures that the output is treated as a literal string, preventing any embedded commands from being executed.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked whether std::cout could execute commands; confirmed that std::cout is a standard output stream that merely writes bytes to the console and does not invoke a shell or execute system commands. No checks or sanitization are required because the sink is not a command executor. The source 'output' is derived from file parsing and string manipulation, but it is never interpreted as a command. Therefore the reported OS Command Injection claim is unfounded.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If 'category' contains a malicious path or command
finding.assumptions: The 'removeLineStartingWith' function is implemented to execute a command or open a file based on the 'category' parameter.

parsed.change_summary: Added a new function `sanitizeInput` to sanitize the 'category' strings before passing them to `removeLineStartingWith`. This function removes any non-alphanumeric characters from the input string.
parsed.how_trigger_is_blocked: The trigger described in the finding no longer works because the 'category' strings are now sanitized before being passed to `removeLineStartingWith`. The `sanitizeInput` function removes any non-alphanumeric characters, preventing any malicious paths or commands from being executed.

parsed.refutation_attempt: 1) Identified that the source variable 'category' is populated from a hard‑coded vector defined at compile time (lines 90‑91). 2) Confirmed that no user‑supplied data (stdin, file, network, argv, env, IPC) feeds into this vector. 3) Noted that the sink function 'removeLineStartingWith' is called with this constant string; without evidence that the function executes external commands, the risk is purely speculative. 4) No other checks or sanitisation are required because the input is not untrusted.
